issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Animal.name: The problem statement (lines 80-86) explicitly instructs that the Animal.name attribute should be a StringBuilder to enable efficient in-place modifications, but the solution defines a field 'private String name;' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java (line 4). This is an attribute type mismatch that will confuse students about the expected field type and the required getters/setters/usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution and template with the problem statement by changing the Animal.name field to type StringBuilder. Update the Animal constructor, getter, and setter to use the StringBuilder field (either have the constructor accept a StringBuilder, or accept a String and internally wrap it with new StringBuilder(...)). Update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) and any usages to match the new field type or constructor behavior so template, solution, and tests are consistent.

issues.description: Constructor de.tum.cit.ase.Animal.Animal(...): The problem statement's requirement to use a StringBuilder for the name implies the constructor should initialize a StringBuilder-backed name field, but the solution's constructor signature is 'public Animal(String name) { this.name = name; }' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java (lines 6-8), which assigns a String to a String field. This mismatches the specification and will force inconsistent subclass constructor calls or field types.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the Animal constructor so it initializes a StringBuilder-backed name field. Options: (a) change the constructor signature to accept a StringBuilder parameter and assign it directly to the field, or (b) keep a String parameter but immediately wrap it (this.name = new StringBuilder(name)) while keeping the field as StringBuilder. Then update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to call super(...) with the appropriate type or rely on the wrapper behavior. Ensure the template, solution, and any tests use the same constructor contract.
